industryContext.contextNote: Handymen perform varied small repair jobs across many client properties, creating broad but generally moderate liability exposure compared to licensed single-trade specialists.

riskFactors.title: Property Damage During Repairs
riskFactors.description: Working across plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and other small repairs increases the chance of accidentally damaging a client's property.

riskFactors.title: Tools & Equipment Loss
riskFactors.description: Handymen carry a wide range of tools between job sites, creating theft and damage exposure that standard property policies don't cover away from a fixed location.

riskFactors.title: Bodily Injury from Varied Tasks
riskFactors.description: Jumping between ladder work, power tools, and manual labor across different trades increases the range of ways a handyman can be injured or cause injury.

faqs.question: Why do handymen need General Liability insurance?
faqs.answer: General Liability covers third-party property damage and bodily injury, which is important given handymen work directly inside and around client properties on varied tasks.

faqs.question: What is the average cost of business insurance for a handyman?
faqs.answer: A handyman in the $0-50k revenue tier pays an estimated $325 per year for baseline General Liability coverage.

faqs.question: Does a handyman need a separate license for electrical or plumbing work?
faqs.answer: Many states restrict handymen from performing licensed electrical or plumbing work beyond minor repairs, and insurance coverage can be affected if unlicensed work exceeds legal limits.

faqs.question: What does a tools and equipment endorsement cover for a handyman?
faqs.answer: It covers the cost to repair or replace tools and equipment if stolen or damaged while being transported between job sites, which a standard property policy typically excludes.

blogContent.whyThisRiskFactor: Handymen carry a 1.6 actuarial risk factor, reflecting broad exposure across multiple minor trades rather than the concentrated risk of a single specialty.
blogContent.howCalculated: Premiums scale with revenue tier, team size, and Tools & Equipment endorsements covering gear transported between job sites.
blogContent.comparisonNote: Handyman premiums sit below licensed single-trade specialists like electricians or plumbers, but above most non-trade small service businesses.
